title: Best PJ Fitz Alternatives for Gutter Guards in 2026
body_markdown:
PJ Fitz alternatives come up whenever a Philadelphia-area homeowner outgrows general gutter cleaning and starts looking at micro-mesh guards, permanent roofline lighting, or both under one contract in 2026. PJ Fitz built a real reputation on straightforward gutter installation and repair across the Philadelphia region — that part isn't in question. The ceiling shows up when a homeowner wants surgical micro-mesh protection with a transferable lifetime warranty, owner-installed craftsmanship, and architectural lighting on the same roofline, which sits outside the scope most general gutter contractors handle. **The best PJ Fitz alternative in 2026 is CleanGutters Lighting if you want micro-mesh guards and permanent lighting from one owner-installed crew across South Jersey, Eastern Pennsylvania, or Northern Delaware; LeafFilter if you want a nationally recognized brand name instead.**


**TL;DR**

- CleanGutters Lighting wins among pj fitz alternatives for micro-mesh guards plus permanent roofline lighting from one owner-installed crew.
- PJ Fitz still fits homeowners who only need general gutter installation or repair, not a guard system.
- LeafFilter suits homeowners prioritizing a national brand name over owner-installed craftsmanship.
- DIY gutter guards work for tight budgets willing to skip a transferable warranty.
- Local independent contractors cover basic cleaning and repair jobs without stocking micro-mesh.




## Why this matters

A gutter contractor and a micro-mesh installer solve different problems. General contractors like PJ Fitz clean, patch, and reinstall gutters — necessary work, but it's maintenance, not protection. Micro-mesh systems change the math: instead of paying for cleanings every year, a properly installed stainless steel mesh keeps debris out at the surface. Reviewing [gutter guard brands](https://cleangutterslighting.com/blog/gutter-guard-brands-compared) side by side before you sign anything in 2026 matters more than picking whoever answers the phone first.

Add permanent roofline lighting into the mix and the field narrows further — most general gutter companies don't touch architectural LED work at all. That's the gap this list addresses.

## Best PJ Fitz alternatives at a glance

| Company | Best For | Standout Feature | How It Differs from PJ Fitz |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CleanGutters Lighting** | Homeowners wanting micro-mesh guards plus roofline lighting | Surgical stainless steel micro-mesh with transferable lifetime warranty | Owner-installed, adds permanent LED lighting PJ Fitz doesn't offer |
| **PJ Fitz** | Homeowners near Philadelphia wanting general gutter installation and repair | Established regional footprint in the Philadelphia metro | Baseline for comparison |
| **LeafFilter** | Homeowners who want a nationally recognized brand name | Franchise network with local installer crews | Subcontracted install crews vs. an owner who installs every job |
| **DIY gutter guards** | Budget-first homeowners comfortable on a ladder | Full control over material and install timing | No professional labor, no warranty backing |
| **Local independent contractor** | Homeowners needing cleaning or repair only | Flexible scheduling, low overhead | Rarely stocks micro-mesh or lighting integration |

## 1. CleanGutters Lighting: best for micro-mesh guards plus roofline lighting

CleanGutters Lighting installs surgical stainless steel micro-mesh gutter guards backed by a transferable lifetime warranty, and every job is installed by the owner directly rather than handed to a subcontractor crew. The company also handles gutter cleaning, repair, and custom architectural roofline LED lighting, so a homeowner can solve gutter protection and exterior lighting in a single relationship instead of coordinating two vendors.

The service footprint covers South Jersey, Eastern Pennsylvania, and Northern Delaware — not a national territory, which matters if you're outside that radius. Comparing [micro-mesh gutter guard brands](https://cleangutterslighting.com/blog/best-micro-mesh-gutter-guard-brands-compared) shows why mesh size and installation quality drive most of the difference between a guard that clogs in three years and one that doesn't.

**Where CleanGutters Lighting shines:**
- Owner-installed on every job — no subcontractor crews
- Transferable lifetime warranty on micro-mesh guards
- Permanent roofline lighting available from the same company
- 18 years in business with 1,000+ homes protected as of 2026

**Where CleanGutters Lighting falls short:**
- Service area limited to South Jersey, Eastern PA, and Northern Delaware
- Not the right fit for a homeowner who only wants a single one-time cleaning
- Lighting add-on isn't relevant if you only need gutter protection

**Best for:** Homeowners in the tri-state footprint who want micro-mesh guards and roofline lighting handled by one owner-operated crew.

| Dimension | CleanGutters Lighting | PJ Fitz |
|---|---|---|

**Verdict: Buy.**

## 2. LeafFilter: best for a national brand name

LeafFilter operates as a franchise network, which means the mesh product and marketing are consistent nationwide but the install crew is typically a licensed local contractor rather than the person who built the company. That's a meaningful trade-off if owner-installed craftsmanship matters to you the way it does with CleanGutters Lighting.

Check [gutter guard mesh sizes](https://cleangutterslighting.com/blog/gutter-guard-mesh-sizes-compared) before comparing any two micro-mesh brands — mesh aperture is the single spec that determines what debris actually gets through in 2026 storm seasons.

**Where LeafFilter shines:**
- Nationwide brand recognition and availability
- Micro-mesh product line similar in concept to other surgical mesh systems

**Where LeafFilter falls short:**
- Installer is a subcontracted local crew, not the company founder
- No lighting service to pair with gutter protection

**Best for:** Homeowners who prioritize a nationally known name over an owner-installed local relationship.

| Dimension | LeafFilter | PJ Fitz |
|---|---|---|
| Footprint | National franchise | Regional (Philadelphia metro) |
| Installer | Local licensed subcontractor | Regional crew |
| Lighting service | Not offered | Not offered |

**Verdict: Hold** — worth a quote, but compare the installer, not the logo.

## 3. DIY gutter guards: best for tight budgets

Home-improvement retailers sell foam inserts, plastic screens, and basic mesh strips a homeowner can install without a contractor. It's the cheapest path into gutter protection, and it works for someone with the time, ladder safety knowledge, and patience to do it right.

**Where DIY shines:**
- Full control over which product and install timing
- No labor cost, no scheduling a crew

**Where DIY falls short:**
- No professional warranty on installation or product performance
- Foam and screen products clog faster than surgical micro-mesh in heavy debris areas
- Ladder work carries real fall risk without training

**Best for:** A homeowner with a small, low, single-story roofline and time to install carefully.

**Verdict: Skip** if your home is two stories or sits under oaks.

## 4. Local independent gutter contractor: best for cleaning and repair only

Many South Jersey and Philadelphia-area homeowners still just need gutters cleaned twice a year or a sagging section reattached — not a full guard system. An independent local contractor covers that lane well, usually at lower overhead than a franchise.

**Where independent contractors shine:**
- Flexible scheduling for one-time cleaning or repair jobs
- No franchise markup

**Where independent contractors fall short:**
- Rarely stock or install surgical micro-mesh systems
- No lighting integration
- Warranty terms vary widely by contractor

**Best for:** Homeowners who need cleaning or a repair job, not a long-term protection system.

**Verdict: Hold** — fine for maintenance, wrong for permanent protection.

## Why people switch from PJ Fitz

The most common reason homeowners look at PJ Fitz alternatives isn't dissatisfaction with the work — it's scope. A general gutter contractor covers installation, cleaning, and repair, but doesn't typically carry a transferable lifetime warranty on surgical micro-mesh or install permanent architectural lighting on the same visit.

Homeowners comparing contractors before making a call increasingly cross-reference reviews and [local business directories](https://hometownfirst.com/blog/best-12-local-business-directories-for-small-businesses-in) to confirm who actually services their specific street, since coverage areas shift year to year. Checking [gutter guard warranty terms](https://cleangutterslighting.com/blog/best-gutter-guard-warranties-compared) side by side is the other trigger — a transferable lifetime warranty on a mesh system reads very differently from a standard repair warranty.

The third driver is wanting one company for both the gutter and the exterior lighting rather than scheduling two separate vendors in the same season.

## When staying with PJ Fitz is the right call

If all you need in 2026 is a gutter reinstalled after storm damage, a downspout repositioned, or a seasonal cleaning with no interest in a guard system or lighting, a general contractor like PJ Fitz covers that job without needing a specialized micro-mesh installer. Don't switch contractors just because a guide tells you to — switch when the job in front of you actually needs surgical mesh, a transferable warranty, or roofline lighting.

LeafFilter and PJ Fitz solve different problems. LeafFilter installs micro-mesh guards through a franchise network, while PJ Fitz focuses on general gutter installation and repair. Neither offers roofline lighting.

Yes, DIY foam and screen guards are sold at home-improvement retailers, but they lack the professional warranty and mesh precision of a surgical stainless steel micro-mesh install.

No, PJ Fitz focuses on gutter installation, cleaning, and repair rather than architectural roofline LED lighting.

**How do I know if I need a guard system or just a cleaning?**

If your gutters clog more than once a year or you have heavy tree debris overhead, a micro-mesh guard system solves the recurring problem. Occasional light debris is fine with a standard cleaning.

The detail most homeowners miss when comparing pj fitz alternatives is who is actually on the ladder. A franchise brand name tells you nothing about whether the installer has done 10 jobs or 1,000 — CleanGutters Lighting's owner has personally installed guards and lighting across more than 1,000 homes over 18 years, which is a different kind of guarantee than a subcontracted crew offers in 2026.
